question.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/20055a4c35ca0fdcb119e69118861d9139d23f404ecb530cf7c1b9ecf39a96d6.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type I regions, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{x}\}\,\cup \,\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{2-x}\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=\sqrt{x}\,⟹\,x={y}^{2}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
y=\sqrt{2-x}\,⟹\,x=2-{y}^{2}.
$$

To change the order of integration we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,{y}^{2}\le x\le 2-{y}^{2}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/77dda47f9036b7019f0d2ea5d72c1b81e5778e5d7108760a3b0394a213690304.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{2}}^{2-{y}^{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
